claims.claim: Assessment is the systematic and dynamic process of collecting and analyzing data about a patient's health; it forms the cornerstone of patient care and serves as the foundation for subsequent nursing care plans.

The American Nurses Association describes assessment as the first step in delivering nursing care — a systematic, dynamic way to collect and analyze data about a client that includes physiological, psychological, sociocultural, spiritual, economic, and lifestyle factors.

The health history is the part of the assessment in which the patient (the primary source) and, when needed, family members provide subjective data — the reason for the visit, current symptoms, medical and surgical history, chronic conditions, medications, allergies, hospitalizations, and lifestyle factors such as diet, exercise, and substance use.

The physical examination is a major part of the initial assessment and uses four techniques to gather objective data: inspection (visually examining the body), palpation (feeling with the hands), percussion (tapping the body and interpreting the sound), and auscultation (listening to body sounds, typically with a stethoscope).

Vital signs such as blood pressure, heart rate, and temperature are measured as part of the initial assessment's physical examination, alongside the head-to-toe exam that systematically evaluates each body system.

Assessments take different forms for different purposes: an initial comprehensive assessment (whose physical exam is conducted head to toe) is performed on admission to establish a baseline; a problem-focused assessment targets a specific problem or complaint; ongoing assessments are performed at regular intervals to monitor progress; OpenStax also names emergency and time-lapsed types.

Assessment data drive the care plan: based on the assessment and diagnosis, the nurse sets measurable goals, and the assessment data, diagnosis, and goals are written into the patient's care plan, which guides implementation and evaluation.

conflictingEvidence.issue: The curriculum groups assessment types as head-to-toe, focused, and ongoing, while OpenStax names five types (initial, problem-focused, ongoing, emergency, time-lapsed).
positions: OpenStax Fundamentals of Nursing Table 12.1 lists initial, problem-focused, ongoing, emergency, and time-lapsed assessments with descriptions and examples.
The curriculum's topic brief and sibling list group the types as head-to-toe, focused, and ongoing.
OpenStax itself describes the initial assessment's physical exam as 'a head-to-toe exam to systematically evaluate each body system.'
conflictingEvidence.resolution: The lesson presents head-to-toe as the comprehensive initial sweep (the format of the initial assessment's physical exam), focused as the problem-focused type, and ongoing as the regular-interval type, which is faithful to the source while matching the curriculum grouping; the lesson notes that the fuller taxonomy also includes emergency and time-lapsed types without teaching them in depth.

conflictingEvidence.issue: Whether vital signs belong to the health history or to the physical exam portion of the assessment.
positions: Some texts group vital signs under a general survey separate from the head-to-toe exam.
OpenStax Fundamentals of Nursing 12.2 lists vital signs (blood pressure, heart rate, temperature) as part of the physical examination during the initial assessment.
conflictingEvidence.resolution: The lesson says vital signs are measured during the assessment as part of the physical examination, and defers technique, ranges, and interpretation to the vital-signs sibling topic, whose own lesson attributes the ranges to OpenStax and MedlinePlus.

conflictingEvidence.issue: Terminology for the asking-the-patient portion: nursing history, health history, patient interview.
positions: OpenStax Fundamentals of Nursing describes the initial assessment's in-depth review of medical and surgical history, medications, allergies, and lifestyle.
OpenStax Clinical Nursing Skills titles a chapter 'Obtaining a Complete Health History.'
conflictingEvidence.resolution: The lesson uses the plain name 'health history' for the asking-the-patient portion and notes the patient is the primary source of this information, matching both OpenStax texts.

unsupportedExistingClaims: The machine-generated placeholder for this topic (generic 'foundational concept in Nursing & Allied Health Foundations' boilerplate with no clinical content, if present in the generated draft store) carried no verifiable clinical substance and was discarded; all content was researched from OpenStax and ANA.

The generated draft's circular vocabulary pattern ('Health Assessment — A foundational Nursing & Allied Health Foundations concept covered in this lesson') was replaced with independently sourced, non-circular definitions.
correctionsNeeded: Attributed the working definition of health assessment to the American Nurses Association as presented in OpenStax Fundamentals of Nursing chapter 12, rather than leaving it unattributed.
Named the four physical exam techniques (inspection, palpation, percussion, auscultation) with one-line descriptions and explicitly marked each as a sibling topic's property.
Connected vital signs to the assessment as measured objective data gathered during the physical exam, deferring technique and ranges to the vital-signs sibling topic.
Used the curriculum grouping (head-to-toe, focused, ongoing) reconciled with OpenStax's five-type taxonomy, with the reconciliation recorded in conflictingEvidence.
All examples are original (Marcus's cough, Ms. Okafor's knee, Mrs. Park's dizziness, Mr. Cruz's blood thinner, Mr. Wu's admission, Amara's clinical day); none are taken from any source.

sourceRecords.title: Fundamentals of Nursing (OpenStax)
sourceRecords.notes: Tier A. Read 2026-08-22 via the Medicine LibreTexts mirror of the OpenStax text: chapter 12 'Assessment — Recognizing Cues', sections 12.1 The Nurse's Role in Assessment, 12.2 Types of Assessment, and 12.3 Collection of Assessment Data (openstax.org itself is JavaScript-rendered and blocks plain fetches; canonical OpenStax URL registered per the phase-4 source registry). Supports: assessment as 'the systematic and dynamic process of collecting and analyzing data about a patient's health' that 'forms the cornerstone of patient care' (citing the American Nurses Association) and serves as the foundation for nursing care plans; the initial assessment's in-depth review of medical and surgical history, chronic conditions, medications, allergies, hospitalizations, surgeries, lifestyle, and social determinants; subjective vs objective data; the patient as the primary data source with family members as secondary sources; the head-to-toe exam as part of the initial assessment's physical examination with vital signs (blood pressure, heart rate, temperature) measured as part of it; the four techniques — inspection, palpation, percussion, auscultation; and the five assessment types (initial, problem-focused, ongoing, emergency, time-lapsed) in Table 12.1. Facts synthesized; no wording reproduced.

sourceRecords.title: The Nursing Process
sourceRecords.notes: Tier B. Read live 2026-08-22 (nursingworld.org served the page directly). Supports: the nursing process as the essential core of registered-nurse practice with five steps — assessment, diagnosis, outcomes/planning, implementation, evaluation; assessment as 'a systematic, dynamic way to collect and analyze data about a client, the first step in delivering nursing care,' covering physiological, psychological, sociocultural, spiritual, economic, and lifestyle factors; and that assessment data, diagnosis, and goals are written into the patient's care plan so the whole team has access to them. Facts synthesized; no wording reproduced.
